requirements.requirement: Run a web application inside a chroot on node1 as the unprivileged appsvc account, serving on port 8080.
requirements.summary: The active process runs as appsvc (UID 993), listens on 0.0.0.0:8080, and returns successful application and health responses. Matching filesystem-device/inode values for /srv/chroot-web and the process root, together with the absence of host /etc/os-release inside that root, directly establish chroot isolation. The same state was observed after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Start the application automatically at boot without requiring an interactive login session.
requirements.summary: The systemd unit was enabled, and a bounded reboot demonstrated recovery under a new boot identity. After boot, the unit was active with a new PID, its journal recorded automatic startup, HTTP checks succeeded, and no interactive login sessions were present. The appsvc account uses /usr/sbin/nologin.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Before and after execution—including after reboot—the node remained CentOS Stream 10 with kernel 6.12.0-205.el10.x86_64. The application uses the platform's existing Python 3 runtime and operated successfully before and after reboot; no package installation or OS/kernel replacement occurred.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct pre-reboot and post-reboot behavioral evidence. The chrooted application runs as the non-login appsvc user on port 8080, starts automatically at boot, responds successfully, and preserves the original CentOS Stream 10 release and kernel. The mandatory node-restart evidence protocol is complete and agrees with the fixed lifecycle boot observations.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands had clear task-related purposes: creating the service account and chroot structure, installing the application, configuring and enabling its hardened systemd unit, opening the required port persistently, and performing the mandatory restart. No unnecessary mutation was identified, reverted or retained. Post-execution observations show no failed services, healthy package-manager state, and only expected reboot-generated private temporary directories; the new port 8080 listener is required by the task. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity, and recovered service, application checksum, chroot, listener, firewall, and HTTP behavior.
